office_worker: Has a standing desk, a sitting desk, and a secret third desk nobody has ever seen.
Replies-all to every email out of pure principle and a little spite.
Owns forty mugs and insists each one has a different personality.
Schedules meetings to plan other meetings, then reschedules both.
Believes the office printer can smell fear and has proof.
Brings a label maker to potlucks and labels the potluck.
Once survived a three-hour budget meeting using only a granola bar and willpower.
Keeps a spare tie in every drawer in case of surprise promotions.
Talks to the office ficus every morning and says it gives better advice than management.
Color-codes the calendar so thoroughly that it now looks like modern art.
Pretends to understand spreadsheets and has fooled everyone for eleven years.
Microwaves fish on Fridays and refuses to apologize.
Wins the office chili cookoff every year with a recipe from a cereal box.
Sends emails at 4 a.m. to seem busy, then naps under the desk at noon.

Wears a headset all day even though nobody has ever called.
Laughs at the boss's jokes a full second early, just to be safe.
Dreams in bullet points and wakes up with action items.
Hid a snack drawer so well that even they can't find it anymore.
Rides the elevator one floor to avoid small talk on the stairs.
Keeps a motivational poster of a cat hanging from a branch, ironically.
Considers the vending machine a close personal friend and a frequent rival.
Gave a forty-slide presentation about reducing the number of slides.
Never takes a lunch break but takes eleven coffee breaks.
Mutes every video call and then talks for ten minutes anyway.
Swears the thermostat is set to "arctic" by a secret office committee.

Fills out expense reports for fun on weekends.

Learned to juggle using only sticky notes and a long quarterly review.
Calls everyone "champ," including the regional manager and the janitor's dog.

Rearranges the desk every Monday to keep the week guessing.
Takes the stairs twice a day and talks about it constantly.
Is the only person who knows how to unjam the copier and charges in cookies.
Writes "per my last email" with the force of a thunderclap.
Can sleep with eyes open during any meeting longer than twenty minutes.
Loves Mondays, and the coworkers are still trying to figure out why.

Counts down to the weekend starting at 9:01 on Monday.
Organized the paperclips by size and is waiting for someone to notice.
Accidentally became the office's unofficial birthday cake coordinator years ago.
Speaks fluent corporate and can say "synergy" without blinking.
bank_teller: Counts every coin twice and every compliment three times, just to be sure.

Keeps a jar of lollipops for kids and a secret jar of better lollipops for adults.

Dreams of the vault at night, mostly about organizing it.

Remembers every customer's dog's name but none of the customers' names.

Practices stamping "PAID" with dramatic flair when nobody is watching.
Treats the coin counting machine like a temperamental racehorse.

barista: Writes customers' names wrong on purpose and calls it performance art.

Has a different apron for every mood and a favorite for Tuesdays.
Steams milk with the intensity of a concert violinist.
Believes every bean has a story and will tell you all of them.

Plays obscure jazz on the shop speakers and dares anyone to complain.
Keeps a tip jar labeled "college fund" and another labeled "chaos fund."

Refuses to drink coffee after noon but makes it until closing.

Hums along to the grinder like it's a favorite song.

Remembers every regular's birthday and sneaks them a free cookie.

Wipes the counter in perfect circles, never squares.
Brews a secret blend for close friends and denies it exists.

Took a pottery class to make the perfect mug and made one terrible bowl.

Wears the name tag upside down on Fridays to see who notices.
Can price-check a melon by weight alone and is usually right.
Believes the self-checkout machines are plotting something.
Keeps a list of the weirdest things ever bought together, and it is long.
Folds shirts so perfectly that customers are afraid to touch them.
Greets every customer with a fun fact about the store's history.
Hums the store radio jingle so often that it's now stuck in everyone's head.
Treats coupon day like a holiday and prepares for it all week.
Pretends the price scanner is a laser blaster when the store is empty.
Loves a good return policy debate more than most people love pizza.
Survived the great glitter spill in aisle seven and still finds sparkles.
Considers the store mascot a close coworker and personal hero.
Thinks the mop bucket has a personality, mostly grumpy.
Collects the rubber bands from vegetable bunches and has a plan for them.
Takes inventory counts very seriously and very loudly.
Gives customers directions by naming nearby snacks.
Practices the perfect receipt fold during lunch breaks.
Tells kids the store cat is the real manager, and the store cat agrees.
Learned to stock shelves blindfolded on a dare and never stopped.
Rates every customer's cart like a judge at a cooking show.
Owns a vest with more pockets than anyone could ever need.
Never forgets a face but always forgets where the mop is.
Swears the frozen aisle is at least ten degrees colder on Tuesdays.
Wins every argument about which register is fastest.
Rearranges the impulse-buy rack to tell a little story every week.
Waves goodbye to every customer, even the grumpy ones, especially the grumpy ones.
Gets genuinely excited about new shipments of tape.

Writes the sale signs in handwriting so fancy nobody can read them.
Tracks the store's busiest hours in a notebook, like a weather scientist.
Remembers the regulars' usual items and quietly sets them aside.

Can parallel park a van in a space meant for a bicycle.
Waves at every dog on the route, and most of the dogs wave back.
Once delivered a package to the wrong house and made a lifelong friend.
Keeps a stash of dog biscuits in the glovebox for diplomatic purposes.
Believes the map app is jealous of their sense of direction.
Sings along to the radio so loudly that customers request songs.
Rings the doorbell exactly once and then waits with heroic patience.
Treats every staircase as a personal fitness challenge.
Carries a clipboard purely for the confidence it brings.
Drives the same route every day but insists it's different each time.
Leaves packages in the most creative hiding spots in the neighborhood.
Swears the hill on Maple Street gets steeper every year.
Wears shorts in every season, including during last winter's snowstorm.
Counts steps every day and has walked to the moon twice, on paper.

Gets along with every cat on the route except one very orange one.
Dreams of a world with no "sorry we missed you" slips.
Times every delivery with a stopwatch and tries to beat yesterday.
Eats lunch in the van with the precision of a racing pit crew.
Never uses the horn, believing it is rude to the street.

Thinks porches tell you everything you need to know about a person.
Stacks boxes so neatly that the warehouse uses photos of them for training.
Rates every doormat on a scale from "welcome" to "go away."
Tells stories about the great box avalanche of last December.
Hums the same three notes all day and nobody knows the song.
Wins the warehouse snack draft every week through careful strategy.
Owns six pairs of the same comfortable shoes and rotates them carefully.
Talks to the packages, telling them to be brave on the journey.
Remembers which houses have the nicest garden gnomes.
Collects unusual return addresses and imagines the senders' lives.
Prefers the scenic route, even when the scenic route is a parking lot.
Survives entirely on gas station coffee and sheer determination.
Practices the gentle porch drop on quiet streets, aiming for a perfect landing.

Considers heavy boxes a compliment from the universe.
Brakes for squirrels, ducks and the occasional confused goose.

Believes kids these days are fine, actually, but loves to grumble anyway.
Gardens with the focus of a chess grandmaster.
Takes a nap every afternoon at exactly 2:15 and calls it a meeting.
Collects postcards from places they have never been.

Bakes cookies for the whole street and expects detailed reviews.
Thinks the mail carrier is the most important person in town.

Calls the hardware store just to chat about bolts.
Spends hours on the bench outside the bakery, people-watching like a pro.
Remembers when this whole district was a cornfield, or claims to.
